title: Hera CEO Jenny Lee's Jaipur Wedding to Indian-Origin Entrepreneur Goes Viral
excerpt: Jenny Lee of healthcare startup Hera and Sagar Jajoo of Silna Health married in a multi-day Jaipur celebration blending Western and Hindu traditions, with her sangeet dance drawing over 700,000 Instagram views.
body:
• Jenny Lee, CEO of New York healthcare startup Hera (valued at around $140 million), married Indian-origin entrepreneur Sagar Jajoo in a multi-day celebration at ITC Mementos Jaipur.
  • The wedding blended Western and Hindu traditions, including a garden-style Christian ceremony, a sangeet, a baraat, pheras, and a black-tie reception.
  • Lee's sangeet performance to K-pop singer Jennie's "Like JENNIE" went viral on Instagram, drawing over 700,000 views.
  • Both Lee and Jajoo are UC Berkeley graduates building healthcare technology companies in New York.

A Cross-Cultural Celebration in Jaipur

Jenny Lee, co-founder and CEO of New York-based healthcare startup Hera, married Sagar Jajoo, an Indian-origin entrepreneur and co-founder of Silna Health, in an elaborate multi-day wedding at Mementos by ITC Hotels in Jaipur. The couple booked the entire property for the celebration, which blended Western and Indian wedding traditions across three days.

https://x.com/ndtv/status/2097105130923720780

Though the wedding took place in October 2025, videos and photos from the event surfaced on social media only recently, turning a private celebration into a viral moment.

Three Days of Ceremonies

The festivities began on October 23 with a welcome lunch, followed by a Western-style wedding conducted as a garden party. Later that evening, an Indian sangeet ceremony brought both families together on the dance floor.

The following day featured a traditional baraat procession and pheras, followed by lunch, cocktails, and a formal black-tie Western reception. The celebrations concluded with an after-party that ran until the early hours of October 25.

The couple's wedding website described the event as an intimate, destination-style celebration, according to IndustryWired.

A Sangeet Performance That Broke the Internet

Lee's sangeet performances became the most talked-about element of the wedding. For the occasion, she danced to "Like JENNIE" by South Korean singer and rapper Jennie, performing at multiple points during the celebrations.

Videos shared by wedding planners Palkan Badlani Weddings & Events showed Lee in three different outfits — a red lehenga, a silver lehenga, and a minidress — bringing energetic confidence to each performance. The planners described her as an exceptionally enthusiastic dancer who needed little convincing to take the floor.

The Instagram video quickly crossed 700,000 views. Comments focused on Lee's confidence and energy, with one viewer summing up the mood: "It's Jenny's world we're living in it."

Two Tech Founders, One Shared Background

Lee and Jajoo share remarkably similar professional trajectories. Both are UC Berkeley graduates who built careers in technology before founding healthcare startups in New York.

Lee studied computer science and business administration at Berkeley and Berkeley Haas. She worked as a software engineering intern at Google, then as a product manager at Dropbox, before becoming a founding product manager at healthcare startup Headway. The idea for Hera came from a personal experience — watching her aunt spend years coordinating care for her grandmother.

"I realized she had silently paid the cost and broken inside as a result of that journey. There was a huge personal sacrifice. It had cost a part of herself."

— Jenny Lee, CEO of Hera, on what inspired her to build the company

Hera helps families navigate the logistics of caring for aging parents, combining care-management expertise with technology to handle appointments, insurance, and healthcare coordination. The company is valued at around $140 million, according to India Weekly.

Jajoo, meanwhile, co-founded Silna Health, a healthcare technology company that helps providers manage prior authorisations, benefit checks, and insurance monitoring. He was previously the first product hire at Truework and a product manager at Blend.

Why It Resonates

The story of two young tech entrepreneurs — one American, one Indian-origin — choosing Jaipur for a wedding that moved fluidly between a garden-party Christian ceremony and traditional Hindu pheras reflects a pattern increasingly common among diaspora couples. India's luxury wedding market, particularly Rajasthan, continues to attract international families seeking celebrations that honour both cultures without compromising on either.

For Lee and Jajoo, the viral moment was unplanned. But the image of a New York CEO in a lehenga, commanding a Jaipur dance floor to a K-pop track, captured something about the ease with which cross-cultural lives are lived now — especially in the Indian-American community.
nri_angle: Two UC Berkeley graduates — one American, one Indian-origin — both building healthcare startups in New York, chose Jaipur for a cross-cultural wedding that blended Christian and Hindu traditions.
